breakthrough: Webhook chaos becomes a dependable programmable event layer
lane: Integration fabric, protocols, and node transport
outcome: Receive, verify, deduplicate, route, replay, and transform events from any provider

phases.name: Phase 1 - Build the Webhook Supernetwork Core

subphases.name: 1.1 Webhook Supernetwork Domain Model and State Plane
work: Define typed entities, capabilities, jobs, events, state transitions, and outputs required to receive, verify, deduplicate, route, replay, and transform events from any provider, with explicit versions and validation at every boundary.

Implement an owned persistent state layer optimized for APIs, protocols, connectors, event streams, transformation, transport, and third-party interoperability; include snapshots or event history when state changes over time.
Expose create, query, update, subscribe, and delete operations through local APIs plus an SDK that never requires private cross-runtime imports.

subphases.name: 1.2 Webhook Supernetwork Execution Runtime
work: Build resumable workers and state machines that perform the core operation: receive, verify, deduplicate, route, replay, and transform events from any provider.
Add cancellation, idempotency, bounded retries, timeouts, quotas, sandbox limits, and deterministic recovery from partial failure.
Create a local simulator that can replay success, malformed inputs, disconnection, overload, provider loss, and restart recovery.

phases.name: Phase 2 - Make Webhook Supernetwork Adaptive and Usable

subphases.name: 2.1 Webhook Supernetwork Decision and Learning Engine
work: Implement scoring, planning, prediction, search, or optimization using schema inference, protocol learning, anomaly repair, stream processing, and semantic transformation.
Create feedback signals from task outcomes and user corrections; update tunable behavior without silently changing hard safety limits.
Return confidence, alternatives, bottlenecks, and a concise machine-readable explanation for every important automated choice.

subphases.name: 2.2 Webhook Supernetwork Interaction Surface
work: Build the primary experience in the visual dataflow canvas, connector lab, live packet map, and integration debugger, including live state, controls, errors, and recovery actions.
Add a CLI and typed client library so humans, agents, games, and third-party applications can operate the capability directly.
Stream progress and intermediate artifacts in real time so long operations remain inspectable, interruptible, and steerable.

phases.name: Phase 3 - Scale Webhook Supernetwork into a Breakthrough Product

subphases.name: 3.1 Webhook Supernetwork Offline, Edge, and Cloud Mesh
work: Implement local-only, hybrid, and cloud execution with explicit capability discovery and graceful behavior when optional peers disappear.
Add conflict-safe synchronization, workload placement, caching, backpressure, and failover across devices or nodes where the feature benefits from distribution.
Benchmark latency, throughput, memory, energy, network transfer, and cost; make the scheduler choose the best execution mode from measured constraints.

subphases.name: 3.2 Webhook Supernetwork Signature Breakthrough
work: Implement the differentiating behavior: Webhook chaos becomes a dependable programmable event layer. Ship it as an opt-in executable mode, not a mockup.
Run adversarial, load, privacy, misuse, degraded-network, and recovery tests against the novel behavior; block unsafe automatic actions.
Package the feature as an independently installable capability with a live demo, sample integration, metrics endpoint, and rollback-safe release artifact.

title: Webhook Supernetwork
